text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/exposed-constant-design-sol.md <<'EOF'
## Problem
The embedded JSON describes three reviewed families. Grouping reparses it on every run, adding transport/schema errors to a fixed domain policy. Preserve membership, preferred display labels, direct evidence, stable minimum UUIDs, and deterministic conflicts while removing the resource and decoder.

## Usage
Existing callers keep `build_funder_groups(&funders)?`. A BBC singleton produces preferred name BBC; alias bridges carry that label to the final minimum UUID component; BBC plus GB News in one component returns the existing conflict error. Persistence still reads `preferred_name.as_str()` and the family key string.

## Shape
Recommend a closed private `ReviewedFamily { Bbc, GbNews, PremierLeague }` enum, deriving Copy/Clone/Eq/Ord. Give it `const ALL: [Self; 3]`, and one exhaustive `const fn definition(self) -> ReviewedFamilyDefinition` returning a private record with `key: &'static str`, `preferred_name: &'static str`, and `names: &'static [&'static str]`. Store each key, display label, and member spellings only in that exhaustive match. ALL enumerates identities, not parallel policy data. This encodes the finite vocabulary and keeps the policy definition together.

Use `Vec<(Uuid, ReviewedFamily)>` and `BTreeSet<ReviewedFamily>` internally instead of unchecked usize indices. Collect family conflicts from enum definitions and sort their keys as today. Move preferred-name selection to a free private function or an associated grouping helper: no FamilyPolicy object remains. Convert constant labels through the existing PreferredFunderName parser when constructing persisted group names; external database parsing continues unchanged. Compile-time policy data is trusted internally; a focused coherence test verifies nonempty unique keys, nonempty labels/member lists, and globally unique normalized member names.

Delete Deserialize from these policy types, FamilyPolicy, PolicyVersion, policy parse function, JSON include_str/file, and PolicyDecode/Policy error variants. Retain PreferredFunderName(String) and TryFrom<String>: outbound grouping also parses database values into it. Derive Deserialize only if another actual consumer needs it; current usage search shows none. Leave normalization, components, matching canonical names rather than aliases, pair evidence, and persistence APIs unchanged.

Interface depth improves because callers see the same single operation while no schema/version machinery reaches the error surface. Types own family identity; grouping owns component conflicts; PreferredFunderName owns external label validity.

## Tradeoffs accepted
- A new family requires an enum variant and ALL entry in exchange for typed internal membership and exhaustive metadata definitions.
- Constants retain the necessary names in the binary, but remove JSON syntax and runtime JSON decoding.

## Alternatives considered
A constant slice of ReviewedFamily structs is slightly shorter and removes the duplicated variant enumeration, but keeps anonymous indices as internal family identities unless references or another identity wrapper are threaded through grouping. The enum gives conflicts and membership a domain type and satisfies the repository finite-vocabulary rule directly.
External input is viable for an operator-configurable policy, but changes deployment and error handling despite the requirement for unchanged behavior.

## Verification
Keep the existing singleton, bridge, direct-evidence, deterministic conflict, and duplicate-identity tests. Replace JSON-schema rejection tests with the policy coherence test plus a behavior loop covering every family's actual member spellings and expected preferred label/key. Keep the preferred-name parser test but remove its JSON missing-field assertion.

## Next implementation step
Replace the JSON model and resource with the enum/definition match, then carry ReviewedFamily through grouping and update only the obsolete tests.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));
